source: CARDI/MAFF Cashew Propagation Guides (compiled from 3 sourced technical documents)
text:
Growing cashew nursery seedlings from seed: collect seed fresh from the current harvest season (roughly February-April), taken from resistant, high-yielding trees. Soak seeds in cool water for 24-48 hours; keep only the seeds that sink (discard floating seeds, which are less viable). Plant sprouted seeds into black nursery bags (roughly 15x30 cm) filled with a soil mix of 1:1:1 regular soil, rice husk ash, and compost, plus about 5 grams of lime per bag, at a planting depth of 2.5 cm. Water regularly; seeds germinate in 15-20 days. Seedlings can be transplanted directly around 3 months old, or used as grafting rootstock at around 30-45 days old.

Grafting (side-veneer/insertion graft, the method most commonly used by Cambodian farmers in Kampong Cham and Kampong Thom provinces): select a scion (the piece to be grafted) from a healthy mother tree, at least 2 months old, green in color, free of pest or disease damage; strip leaves from the chosen scion branch 1-2 weeks before cutting it for grafting. On the rootstock seedling, cut the top off leaving about 15 cm of stem above soil level, keeping the bottom 2 pairs of leaves; split the cut stem down the center to a depth of about 3-5 cm. Cut a 10-15 cm scion piece from the mother tree and shape its base into a V roughly 3-5 cm long. Insert the shaped scion into the split rootstock so the bark layers align and overlap on at least one side. Wrap the graft union tightly with thin plastic (nursery-grafting plastic) to seal out water and prevent moisture loss, covering all the way to the tip of the scion. Keep grafted plants in a shaded area for 15 days afterward; remove any new shoots sprouting from the rootstock itself. Remove the plastic wrap after 3-4 months, after which the grafted plant is ready for field planting.
